exam: UGC NET CSE | June 2012 | Part 2 | Question: 2
question: The post order traversal of a binary tree is DEBFCA. Find out the pre-order traversal
explanation:
In binary tree traversal:
• Pre-order: Visit Root → Left Subtree → Right Subtree.
• In-order: Visit Left Subtree → Root → Right Subtree.
• Post-order: Visit Left Subtree → Right Subtree → Root.
Given the post-order sequence, the last element is always the tree root. By finding the root in the in-order/pre-order sequence, we can recursively determine left and right subtrees. Hence, Option C ("ABDECF") is the correct preorder traversal.

question: Consider the following statements: i . Depth-first search is used to traverse a rooted tree ii . Pre-order, Post-order and Inorder are used to list the vertices of an ordered rooted tree. iii . Huffman's algorithm is used to find an optimal binary tree with given weights iv . Topological sorting provides a labelling such that the parents have larger labels than their children Which one of the above statements is true?
explanation:
In binary tree traversal:
• Pre-order: Visit Root → Left Subtree → Right Subtree.
• In-order: Visit Left Subtree → Root → Right Subtree.
• Post-order: Visit Left Subtree → Right Subtree → Root.
Given the post-order sequence, the last element is always the tree root. By finding the root in the in-order/pre-order sequence, we can recursively determine left and right subtrees. Hence, Option D  is the correct preorder traversal.

question: bcnf-decomposition
explanation:
In database normalization:
• A relation is in BCNF if for every non-trivial functional dependency X → Y, X is a superkey.
• 3NF allows X to be a superkey OR Y to be a prime attribute.
• Every relation in BCNF is guaranteed to be in 3NF, but not vice-versa. Lossless join decomposition is always achievable in 3NF and BCNF, though BCNF may not always preserve all functional dependencies. Option B is the correct formulation.

exam: UGC NET CSE | December 2012 | Part 3 | Question: 63
question: The third normal form is based on the concept of_____
explanation:
In database normalization:
• A relation is in BCNF if for every non-trivial functional dependency X → Y, X is a superkey.
• 3NF allows X to be a superkey OR Y to be a prime attribute.
• Every relation in BCNF is guaranteed to be in 3NF, but not vice-versa. Lossless join decomposition is always achievable in 3NF and BCNF, though BCNF may not always preserve all functional dependencies. Option B is the correct formulation.

question: Consider the traversal of a tree Preorder Inorder Which of the following is correct post order traversal?
explanation:
In binary tree traversal:
• Pre-order: Visit Root → Left Subtree → Right Subtree.
• In-order: Visit Left Subtree → Root → Right Subtree.
• Post-order: Visit Left Subtree → Right Subtree → Root.
Given the post-order sequence, the last element is always the tree root. By finding the root in the in-order/pre-order sequence, we can recursively determine left and right subtrees. Hence, Option C  is the correct preorder traversal.

explanation:
Under virtual memory management:
• FIFO replaces the oldest page in memory and can suffer from Belady's Anomaly (increasing frames can increase page faults).
• LRU (Least Recently Used) replaces the page unused for the longest time and does not suffer from Belady's anomaly (stack algorithm).
• Effective memory access time (EMAT) = Hit_Ratio × (TLB + Mem) + (1 - Hit_Ratio) × (TLB + 2 × Mem + Fault_Penalty). Option B is correct.

explanation:
Under virtual memory management:
• FIFO replaces the oldest page in memory and can suffer from Belady's Anomaly (increasing frames can increase page faults).
• LRU (Least Recently Used) replaces the page unused for the longest time and does not suffer from Belady's anomaly (stack algorithm).
• Effective memory access time (EMAT) = Hit_Ratio × (TLB + Mem) + (1 - Hit_Ratio) × (TLB + 2 × Mem + Fault_Penalty). Option B is correct.

explanation:
Under virtual memory management:
• FIFO replaces the oldest page in memory and can suffer from Belady's Anomaly (increasing frames can increase page faults).

question: A virtual memory has a page size of words. There are eight pages and four blocks. The associative memory page table contains the following entries : Which of the following list of virtual addresses (in decimal) will not cause any page fault if referenced by the CPU?
explanation:
Under virtual memory management:
• FIFO replaces the oldest page in memory and can suffer from Belady's Anomaly (increasing frames can increase page faults).
• LRU (Least Recently Used) replaces the page unused for the longest time and does not suffer from Belady's anomaly (stack algorithm).
• Effective memory access time (EMAT) = Hit_Ratio × (TLB + Mem) + (1 - Hit_Ratio) × (TLB + 2 × Mem + Fault_Penalty). Option C is correct.

exam: UGC NET CSE | June 2013 | Part 2 | Question: 13
question: Which normal form is considered as adequate for usual database design?
explanation:
In database normalization:
• A relation is in BCNF if for every non-trivial functional dependency X → Y, X is a superkey.
• 3NF allows X to be a superkey OR Y to be a prime attribute.
• Every relation in BCNF is guaranteed to be in 3NF, but not vice-versa. Lossless join decomposition is always achievable in 3NF and BCNF, though BCNF may not always preserve all functional dependencies. Option B is the correct formulation.

question: Which type of coupling is least preferred ?
explanation:
In software engineering modular design principles:

question: Preorder is also known as:
explanation:
In binary tree traversal:
• Pre-order: Visit Root → Left Subtree → Right Subtree.
• In-order: Visit Left Subtree → Root → Right Subtree.
• Post-order: Visit Left Subtree → Right Subtree → Root.
Given the post-order sequence, the last element is always the tree root. By finding the root in the in-order/pre-order sequence, we can recursively determine left and right subtrees. Hence, Option C  is the correct preorder traversal.

explanation:
Under virtual memory management:
• FIFO replaces the oldest page in memory and can suffer from Belady's Anomaly (increasing frames can increase page faults).
• LRU (Least Recently Used) replaces the page unused for the longest time and does not suffer from Belady's anomaly (stack algorithm).
• Effective memory access time (EMAT) = Hit_Ratio × (TLB + Mem) + (1 - Hit_Ratio) × (TLB + 2 × Mem + Fault_Penalty). Option B is correct.

question: If a relation is in 2NF and 3NF forms then :

options.A: no non-prime attribute is functionally dependent on other non-prime attributes
options.B: no non-prime attribute is functionally dependent on prime attributes
options.D: prime attribute is functionally independent of all non-prime attributes

explanation:
In database normalization:
• A relation is in BCNF if for every non-trivial functional dependency X → Y, X is a superkey.
• 3NF allows X to be a superkey OR Y to be a prime attribute.
• Every relation in BCNF is guaranteed to be in 3NF, but not vice-versa. Lossless join decomposition is always achievable in 3NF and BCNF, though BCNF may not always preserve all functional dependencies. Option B is the correct formulation.

explanation:
In binary tree traversal:
• Pre-order: Visit Root → Left Subtree → Right Subtree.
• In-order: Visit Left Subtree → Root → Right Subtree.
• Post-order: Visit Left Subtree → Right Subtree → Root.
Given the post-order sequence, the last element is always the tree root. By finding the root in the in-order/pre-order sequence, we can recursively determine left and right subtrees. Hence, Option C  is the correct preorder traversal.

question: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion and the other is labelled as Reason .A virtual memory system uses first-in first-out page replacement policy and allocates a fixed number of frames to a process Assertion : Increasing number of page frames allocated to a process sometimes increases the page fault rate. Reason : Some programs do not exhibit locality of reference. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.A: Both and are true and is the correct explanation of
options.B: Both and are true but is NOT the correct explanation of

explanation:
Under virtual memory management:
• FIFO replaces the oldest page in memory and can suffer from Belady's Anomaly (increasing frames can increase page faults).
• LRU (Least Recently Used) replaces the page unused for the longest time and does not suffer from Belady's anomaly (stack algorithm).
• Effective memory access time (EMAT) = Hit_Ratio × (TLB + Mem) + (1 - Hit_Ratio) × (TLB + 2 × Mem + Fault_Penalty). Option B is correct.

question: Consider the following statements: i . A database design is in BCNF if each member of the set of relation schemas that constitutes the design is in BCNF ii . A BCNF schema can have transitive dependency iii . It is always possible to obatin a design without sacrificing a lossless join There are multivalued dependencies in
explanation:
In database normalization:
• A relation is in BCNF if for every non-trivial functional dependency X → Y, X is a superkey.
• 3NF allows X to be a superkey OR Y to be a prime attribute.
• Every relation in BCNF is guaranteed to be in 3NF, but not vice-versa. Lossless join decomposition is always achievable in 3NF and BCNF, though BCNF may not always preserve all functional dependencies. Option B is the correct formulation.

exam: UGC NET CSE | June 2011 | Part 2 | Question: 22
question: Given a binary tree whose inorder and preorder traversal are given by Inorder : EICFBGDJHK Preorder : BCEIFDGHJK The post order traversal of the above binary tree is

options.A: I E F C G J K H D B
options.B: I E F C J G K H D B
options.C: I E F C G K J H D B
options.D: I E F C G J K D B H

explanation:
In binary tree traversal:
• Pre-order: Visit Root → Left Subtree → Right Subtree.
• In-order: Visit Left Subtree → Root → Right Subtree.
• Post-order: Visit Left Subtree → Right Subtree → Root.
Given the post-order sequence, the last element is always the tree root. By finding the root in the in-order/pre-order sequence, we can recursively determine left and right subtrees. Hence, Option C  is the correct preorder traversal.

exam: UGC NET CSE | June 2019 | Part 1 | Question: 11
question: Michaelangelo is famous for having successfully interpreted the human body. His great achievement is that of the painting of David whose hands reach out as a sign of human capability and potential. It is assumed that the time he lived was ripe for exchange of knowledge, development in science and matured enough to advance the horizon of investigation in all fields. Renaissance humanism stressed on a serious rethink on the nature of art that focussed on accurate details. In painting and sculpture, artists focussed on not so casual but verifiable and minute details. Michaelangelo’s paintings are no exception to it. In a study published in the journal of the Royal Society of medicine, a group of surgeons are of the opinion that the great master was “afflicted by an illness involving his joints”. They have used his portraits as evidence to argue their view. During his life, he complained of what he felt to be ‘gout’. Later he complained of his sore and stiff hands which the doctors would find to be natural for someone who was engaged in handmade art. The doctors found corroboration of those claims in portraits of the artist that show a hanging left hand with both degenerative and non-degenerative changes. They attribute the pain not just to arthritis, but to the stress of hammering and chiselling and note that though the master was seen hammering days before his death at an old age, he did not write or sign his own letters before his death. In recent times there have been attempts to diagnose famous artists with diseases that were not known during their time. This practice has raised many questions, especially on the issue of ethics in research. It is also inferred from authentic analysis that Michaelangelo persisted in his work until his last days. This theory would emphasize that his artistic subject defined his physical infirmities. Michaelangelo lived during a time that lets us know that

options.A: Human aspirants are limitless and open to new vistas of knowledge
options.B: Cross cultural exchange in ideas is the only way for human progress
options.C: It is progress of science and anatomy that contributes to civilizations exclusively
options.D: Human beings possess language which is the only key to knowledge

explanation:
According to standard UGC NET Computer Science official answer key and concepts:
Option A ("Human aspirants are limitless and open to new vistas of knowledge") is the correct answer for this question from Others: Others (General Awareness). This question tests fundamental principles and analytical techniques standard in UGC NET syllabus.

exam: UGC NET CSE | August 2016 | Part 2 | Question: 18
question: Consider the following statements regarding relational database model : (a) NULL values can be used to opt a tuple out of enforcement of a foreign key. (b) Suppose that table T has only one candidate key. If Q is in NF, then it is also in BCNF. (c) The difference between the project operator in relational algebra and the SELECT keyword in SQL is that if the resulting table/set has more than one occurrences of the same tuple, then will return only one of them, while SQL SELECT will return all. One can determine that :
explanation:
In database normalization:
• A relation is in BCNF if for every non-trivial functional dependency X → Y, X is a superkey.
• 3NF allows X to be a superkey OR Y to be a prime attribute.
• Every relation in BCNF is guaranteed to be in 3NF, but not vice-versa. Lossless join decomposition is always achievable in 3NF and BCNF, though BCNF may not always preserve all functional dependencies. Option B is the correct formulation.

explanation:
In binary tree traversal:
• Pre-order: Visit Root → Left Subtree → Right Subtree.
• In-order: Visit Left Subtree → Root → Right Subtree.
• Post-order: Visit Left Subtree → Right Subtree → Root.
Given the post-order sequence, the last element is always the tree root. By finding the root in the in-order/pre-order sequence, we can recursively determine left and right subtrees. Hence, Option C  is the correct preorder traversal.

exam: UGC NET CSE | Junet 2015 | Part 2 | Question: 23
question: Level order Traversal of a rooted Tree can be done by starting from root and performing:
explanation:
In binary tree traversal:
• Pre-order: Visit Root → Left Subtree → Right Subtree.
• In-order: Visit Left Subtree → Root → Right Subtree.
• Post-order: Visit Left Subtree → Right Subtree → Root.
Given the post-order sequence, the last element is always the tree root. By finding the root in the in-order/pre-order sequence, we can recursively determine left and right subtrees. Hence, Option A ("Breadth First Search") is the correct preorder traversal.

• TCP is connection-oriented with flow & congestion control, while UDP is connectionless. Option A correctly matches the specification.

• Cohesion should be HIGH (Functional cohesion is the strongest and most desirable).
